ibps_po_rc.title: Reading Comprehension — Questions 1 to 8
ibps_po_rc.content:
India's Account Aggregator (AA) framework, licensed by the Reserve Bank of India, has quietly re-engineered how individuals and micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) share financial records with lenders. Under traditional paper-based underwriting, small merchants had to assemble physical bank statements, GST returns, and notarized collateral documents—a cumbersome process that frequently pushed creditworthy borrowers toward informal moneylenders charging punitive rates.

By contrast, the Account Aggregator ecosystem operates strictly on explicit, revocable digital consent. Acting as data-blind conduits, aggregators transfer encrypted cash-flow information directly from Financial Information Providers (such as commercial banks, insurers, and pension funds) to Financial Information Users (such as lending institutions and wealth managers) without storing or reading the underlying data. Because loan assessment can now rely on verified, real-time digital cash flows rather than solely on immovable property collateral, underwriting turnaround times for small business loans have shrunk from weeks to minutes.

Nevertheless, industry analysts emphasize that universal adoption demands more than elegant architecture. Rural borrowers often lack awareness of consent dashboards and may inadvertently authorize overly broad data-sharing durations. Regulators and banks must therefore invest in intuitive vernacular consent prompts, transparent audit trails, and swift grievance redressal mechanisms so that consent-driven open finance remains both inclusive and **resilient**.

ibps_po_cloze.title: Cloze Test — Questions 9 to 14
ibps_po_cloze.content:
In the following passage, certain words have been omitted. Choose the most contextually appropriate option for each numbered blank.

Central banks across emerging economies face a delicate balancing act whenever global commodity prices __(9)__ abruptly. Raising policy interest rates helps __(10)__ inflationary expectations and defend domestic currency stability, yet excessively tight monetary conditions can __(11)__ private capital expenditure and slow job creation. Consequently, policymakers increasingly supplement interest-rate decisions with transparent forward __(12)__ so that commercial banks and bond markets can adjust smoothly without triggering panic. Over the long run, coordinated fiscal discipline and supply-side __(13)__ remain indispensable to sustaining non-inflationary __(14)__.

ibps_po_pj.title: Para Jumble — Questions 20 to 24
ibps_po_pj.content:
Rearrange the following FIVE sentences (A), (B), (C), (D), and (E) in the proper sequence to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph, then answer Questions 20 to 24:

**(A)** Recognizing this gap, several coastal municipalities have begun restoring native mangrove belts along vulnerable estuaries.
**(B)** Over the past two decades, unplanned shoreline construction has stripped away natural storm barriers across many tropical deltas.
**(C)** Early hydrological audits already show that these replanted mangroves cut incoming wave energy by more than half while reviving local fisheries.
**(D)** As a result, even moderate cyclonic surges now inundate farmland and residential neighbourhoods several kilometres inland.
**(E)** Beyond protecting infrastructure, community-led nurseries also create steady seasonal income for local fishing households.

ibps_po_p1.title: Puzzle 1 (Linear Seating) — Questions 1 to 5 (Reasoning)
ibps_po_p1.content:
Study the following information carefully and answer Questions 1 to 5:

Eight persons — **A, B, C, D, E, F, G, and H** — are sitting in a straight horizontal row facing North (not necessarily in the same order).
- **A** sits third from the left end.
- Exactly three persons sit between **A** and **F**.
- **E** sits immediately to the right of **F**.
- **D** sits second to the left of **F**.
- **B** sits immediately between **D** and **F**.
- **C** sits at one of the extreme ends of the row.
- **G** sits immediately to the right of **C**.

ibps_po_p2.title: Puzzle 2 (Circular Seating) — Questions 6 to 10 (Reasoning)
ibps_po_p2.content:
Study the following information carefully and answer Questions 6 to 10:

Eight friends — **P, Q, R, S, T, U, V, and W** — are seated around a circular table facing the centre (not necessarily in the same order).
- **S** sits directly opposite to **P**.
- **R** sits second to the left of **P**.
- **T** sits immediately to the right of **P**.
- **Q** sits third to the right of **P**.
- **V** sits immediately between **T** and **Q**.
- **W** sits immediately to the right of **S**.
- **U** is not an immediate neighbour of **S**.

ibps_po_p3.title: Puzzle 3 (Floor-Based Puzzle) — Questions 11 to 15 (Reasoning)
ibps_po_p3.content:
Study the following information carefully and answer Questions 11 to 15:

Eight people — **J, K, L, M, N, O, P, and Q** — live on eight different floors of a building numbered **1** (ground floor) to **8** (top floor), one person per floor.
- **M** lives on Floor 4.
- Exactly two persons live between **M** and **O**, and **O** lives above **M**.
- **Q** lives immediately above **O**.
- **L** lives immediately below **O**.
- **P** lives immediately above **M**, while **J** lives immediately below **M**.
- **K** lives on the ground floor (Floor 1).

ibps_po_p4.title: Puzzle 4 (Day-Based Schedule) — Questions 16 to 20 (Reasoning)

- **Economics** is scheduled on the last day of the week.
- **Chemistry** is scheduled immediately after **Maths**.
- **English** is scheduled immediately after **Physics**.
- **History** is scheduled immediately before **Maths**.

questions.question: Why did small merchants often turn to informal moneylenders under traditional paper-based underwriting?
options: Informal lenders offered government subsidies on GST filings
Assembling physical statements, returns, and notarized collateral was cumbersome and slow
Commercial banks were legally prohibited from lending to MSMEs
Account Aggregators charged higher fees than moneylenders
Digital consent dashboards were mandatory since 1995
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 explains that assembling physical bank statements, GST returns, and notarized collateral documents was cumbersome, pushing creditworthy borrowers to informal lenders.

questions.question: In the Account Aggregator ecosystem, what does the phrase 'data-blind conduits' imply?
options: Aggregators permanently store customer passwords on public servers
Aggregators reject all encrypted financial documents
Aggregators transmit encrypted financial data without reading or storing its contents
Aggregators can share user data without taking digital consent
Aggregators issue physical passbooks instead of digital files
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 states that data-blind conduits transfer encrypted cash-flow data directly without storing or reading the underlying information.

questions.question: What has enabled loan underwriting turnaround times for small businesses to shrink from weeks to minutes?
options: Elimination of all regulatory oversight by RBI
Reliance on verified, real-time digital cash flows instead of solely immovable collateral
Replacing all commercial banks with unregulated peer apps
Mandatory branch visits twice a week by borrowers
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 explicitly links faster turnaround times to assessing verified real-time digital cash flows rather than solely immovable collateral.

questions.question: Which of the following is mentioned as an example of a Financial Information User (FIU) in the passage?
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 identifies lending institutions and wealth managers as Financial Information Users (FIUs).

questions.question: What specific risk for rural borrowers is highlighted in the final paragraph?
options: They cannot open savings accounts in public sector banks
They may unintentionally authorize overly broad data-sharing durations due to low awareness
They are excluded from all RBI licensing policies
They refuse to accept digital loan disbursements
They face mandatory physical collateral audits every month
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 notes that rural borrowers often lack awareness of consent dashboards and may inadvertently authorize overly broad data-sharing durations.

questions.question: Which measures do analysts recommend to make consent-driven open finance inclusive?
options: Vernacular consent prompts, transparent audit trails, and swift grievance redressal
Higher collateral margins and longer processing queues
Restricting AA access strictly to English-speaking metro users
questions.explanation: The final sentence recommends intuitive vernacular consent prompts, transparent audit trails, and swift grievance redressal mechanisms.

questions.question: Which word is MOST SIMILAR in meaning to `RESILIENT` as highlighted in the passage?
questions.explanation: 'Resilient' means strong, adaptable, and able to withstand shocks — closest to 'Robust'.

questions.question: Which word is MOST OPPOSITE in meaning to `CUMBERSOME` as used in the opening paragraph?
questions.explanation: 'Cumbersome' means slow, complicated, and unwieldy; its opposite is 'Streamlined' (efficient and simple).

questions.question: Choose the most appropriate word for blank (9).
questions.explanation: Commodity prices 'surge' abruptly, creating inflationary pressure.

questions.question: Choose the most appropriate word for blank (10).
questions.explanation: Central banks raise policy rates to 'anchor' inflationary expectations.

questions.question: Choose the most appropriate word for blank (11).
questions.explanation: Excessively tight monetary conditions can 'dampen' (slow down) private capital expenditure.

questions.question: Choose the most appropriate word for blank (12).
questions.explanation: 'Forward guidance' is the standard central banking communication tool.

questions.question: Choose the most appropriate word for blank (13).
questions.explanation: 'Supply-side reforms' pair with fiscal discipline to curb structural inflation.

questions.question: Choose the most appropriate word for blank (14).
questions.explanation: 'Sustaining non-inflationary growth' is the standard macroeconomic objective.

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error:
`(A) The board of directors / (B) have decided to / (C) expand its retail branches / (D) across eastern India. / (E) No error`
questions.explanation: 'The board of directors' acts as a single unified body here (confirmed by 'its'), so singular verb `has decided` should replace `have decided`.

questions.question:
Identify the part with an error:
`(A) Hardly had the branch opened / (B) than a long queue / (C) of pension holders formed / (D) outside the counter. / (E) No error`
questions.explanation: `Hardly` pairs with `when` (not `than`): `Hardly had the branch opened when...`.

questions.question:
Identify the part with an error:
`(A) Despite of repeated reminders / (B) from the audit team, / (C) the regional office failed / (D) to submit the vouchers. / (E) No error`
questions.explanation: `Despite` is never followed by `of` (use either `Despite repeated reminders` or `In spite of repeated reminders`).

questions.question:
Identify the part with an error:
`(A) Neither the CFO / (B) nor the senior auditors / (C) was able to explain / (D) the sudden discrepancy. / (E) No error`
questions.explanation: With `neither...nor`, the verb agrees with the nearer subject (`senior auditors`, plural): `were able to explain`.

questions.question:
Identify the part with an error:
`(A) The new digital kiosk / (B) enables customers / (C) to update their passbooks / (D) within two minutes. / (E) No error`
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically and idiomatically correct (No error).

questions.question: Which of the following should be the **FIRST** sentence after rearrangement?
questions.explanation: Correct sequence: **B-D-A-C-E**. Sentence B introduces the core issue (unplanned shoreline construction stripping storm barriers).

questions.question: Which of the following should be the **SECOND** sentence after rearrangement?
questions.explanation: Sequence **B-D-A-C-E**: Sentence D ('As a result...') states the immediate consequence of B.

questions.question: Which of the following should be the **THIRD** sentence after rearrangement?
questions.explanation: Sequence **B-D-A-C-E**: Sentence A ('Recognizing this gap...') introduces the restoration response.

questions.question: Which of the following should be the **FOURTH** sentence after rearrangement?
questions.explanation: Sequence **B-D-A-C-E**: Sentence C provides early hydrological evidence on 'these replanted mangroves'.

questions.question: Which of the following should be the **FIFTH (LAST)** sentence after rearrangement?
questions.explanation: Sequence **B-D-A-C-E**: Sentence E ('Beyond protecting infrastructure...') adds the concluding co-benefit.

questions.question:
In the sentence below, four bold words (A–D) may be misplaced. Choose the pair to swap so the sentence becomes meaningful:
`The central bank **trimmed** (A) liquidity measures to **inflation** (B) credit flow while keeping **curb** (C) strictly under **watch** (D).`
questions.explanation: Swapping B and C gives: '...trimmed liquidity measures to **curb** credit flow while keeping **inflation** strictly under watch.'

questions.question:
Choose the pair of bold words to interchange to make the sentence contextually correct:
`Automated fraud **alerts** (A) help banks **detect** (B) suspicious card **transactions** (C) within **milliseconds** (D).`
questions.explanation: All four words are already in their correct contextual positions.

questions.question: To ______ rural credit penetration, banks must ______ simplified KYC workflows for small farmers.
questions.explanation: 'Accelerate rural credit penetration' pairs logically with 'adopt simplified KYC workflows'.

questions.question: Although quarterly revenues ______ expectations, rising input costs slightly ______ net operating margins.
questions.explanation: 'Although' signals contrast: revenues 'exceeded' expectations, yet rising costs 'compressed' margins.

questions.question:
Which phrase should replace the bracketed segment to make the sentence grammatically correct?
`Had she reviewed the ledger carefully, she (will have noticed) the duplicate entry.`
questions.explanation: Third conditional (`Had + S + V3`) requires `would have + V3` in the main clause.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the bracketed phrase:
`The committee looks forward (to meet) the fintech founders next Monday.`
questions.explanation: `Look forward to` takes a gerund (`-ing` form): `looks forward to meeting`.

questions.question: What is the total home loan amount disbursed by **SBI** across all five months combined?
What is the ratio of total loans disbursed by **PNB** in all five months to that by **BOB** in all five months?
What is the average loan disbursed per bank in the month of **March**?
questions.explanation: March total = $120 + 70 + 80 + 90 = 360$. Average across 4 banks = $360 / 4 = ₹90\text{ Crore}$.

questions.question: The loan disbursed by **SBI** in March is what percent MORE than the loan disbursed by **Canara Bank** in April?
questions.explanation: SBI Mar = 120, Canara Apr = 80. Percent more = $\frac{120 - 80}{80} \times 100 = 50\%$.

questions.question: What is the difference between the total loans disbursed by all four banks in **May** and in **January**?
How many **male** employees work in the **IT** and **Sales** departments together?
questions.explanation: IT males = $\frac{5}{8}\times 240 = 150$. Sales males = $\frac{7}{10}\times 300 = 210$. Sum = $150 + 210 = 360$.

questions.question: Find the total number of **female** employees across all five departments combined.
questions.explanation: Females: IT=90, HR=90, Sales=90, Finance=100, Operations=100. Total = $90+90+90+100+100 = 470$.

questions.question: Female employees in **Finance** are what percent of male employees in **Operations**?
questions.explanation: Finance females = $\frac{5}{9}\times 180 = 100$. Operations males = $\frac{3}{5}\times 250 = 150$. Percentage = $\frac{100}{150}\times 100 = 66\frac{2}{3}\%$.

questions.question: What is the ratio of **male** employees in **HR** to **male** employees in **Finance**?
questions.explanation: HR males = $\frac{2}{5}\times 150 = 60$. Finance males = $\frac{4}{9}\times 180 = 80$. Ratio = $60:80 = 3:4$.

questions.question: By how many is the total number of **male** employees across the whole company greater than the total number of **female** employees?
questions.explanation: Total males = $150+60+210+80+150 = 650$. Total females = $470$. Difference = $650 - 470 = 180$.

Find the missing number in the series:
`14, 15, 32, 99, 400, ?`
questions.explanation: Pattern: $\times 1+1, \times 2+2, \times 3+3, \times 4+4, \times 5+5$: $400 \times 5 + 5 = 2005$.

questions.question:
Find the missing number in the series:
`18, 27, 45, 72, 108, ?`
questions.explanation: Differences are $+9, +18, +27, +36$, so next difference is $+45$: $108 + 45 = 153$.

questions.question:
Find the missing number in the series:
`640, 320, 160, 80, 40, ?`
questions.explanation: Each term is halved ($\div 2$): $40 \div 2 = 20$.

questions.question:
Find the WRONG number in the following series:
`11, 13, 17, 25, 41, 74, 137`

Find the missing number in the series:
`5, 6, 10, 19, 35, ?`
questions.explanation: Differences are consecutive squares $+1^2, +2^2, +3^2, +4^2, +5^2$: $35 + 25 = 60$.

questions.question:
Solve both equations and choose the correct relationship between $x$ and $y$:
I. $x^2 - 9x + 20 = 0$
II. $y^2 - 6y + 8 = 0$
options: $x = y$ or relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation: I: $(x-4)(x-5)=0 \Rightarrow x = 4, 5$. II: $(y-2)(y-4)=0 \Rightarrow y = 2, 4$. Hence $x \ge y$.

questions.question:
Determine the relation between $x$ and $y$:
I. $x^2 + 7x + 12 = 0$
II. $y^2 + 3y + 2 = 0$
questions.explanation: I: $x = -3, -4$. II: $y = -1, -2$. Every root of $x$ is strictly less than every root of $y \Rightarrow x < y$.

questions.question:
Determine the relation between $x$ and $y$:
I. $2x^2 - 11x + 15 = 0$
II. $y^2 - 9y + 20 = 0$
questions.explanation: I: $(2x-5)(x-3)=0 \Rightarrow x = 2.5, 3$. II: $y = 4, 5$. Thus $x < y$.

questions.question:
Determine the relation between $x$ and $y$:
I. $x^2 = 49$
II. $y^2 - 14y + 49 = 0$
questions.explanation: I: $x = +7, -7$. II: $(y-7)^2 = 0 \Rightarrow y = 7$. Hence $x \le y$.

questions.question:
Determine the relation between $x$ and $y$:
I. $x^2 - 5x - 14 = 0$
II. $y^2 - 3y - 10 = 0$
questions.explanation: I: $x = 7, -2$. II: $y = 5, -2$. Since $7 > 5$ and $-2 < 5$, no fixed inequality holds.

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 14 km/h and the speed of the current is 2 km/h. How long will it take to travel 48 km downstream and 36 km upstream?
questions.explanation: Downstream = $16\text{ km/h}$ ($48/16 = 3$ h); Upstream = $12\text{ km/h}$ ($36/12 = 3$ h). Total = $6$ hours.

questions.question: P started a business with ₹30,000. After 4 months, Q joined with ₹45,000. At the end of the year, they earned a total profit of ₹42,000. Find Q's share.
A vessel contains 60 litres of milk and water in the ratio $3 : 2$. If 10 litres of mixture are removed and replaced with 10 litres of pure milk, what is the new ratio of milk to water?
questions.explanation: After removing 10 L, 50 L remain: 30 L milk, 20 L water. Adding 10 L milk gives 40 L milk and 20 L water ⇒ ratio $2 : 1$.

questions.question: A and B together can complete a task in 10 days, while A alone can finish it in 15 days. In how many days can B alone complete the task?
questions.explanation: Work = 30 units. A+B = 3/day, A = 2/day ⇒ B = 1/day ⇒ B takes 30 days.

questions.question: A merchant sells two chairs for ₹1,200 each, gaining 20% on the first and losing 20% on the second. What is his overall percentage profit or loss?
questions.explanation: Equal SP with $+x\%$ and $-x\%$ always yields a loss of $\frac{x^2}{100}\% = \frac{400}{100}\% = 4\%$ loss.

questions.question: A sum of ₹12,500 amounts to ₹15,125 in 2 years at compound interest compounded annually. Find the annual rate of interest.
questions.explanation: $\left(1 + \frac{R}{100}\right)^2 = \frac{15125}{12500} = \frac{121}{100} \Rightarrow 1 + \frac{R}{100} = 1.1 \Rightarrow R = 10\%$.

questions.question: A 220 m long train passes a 280 m long tunnel in 25 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanation: Distance = $220 + 280 = 500\text{ m}$. Speed = $500/25 = 20\text{ m/s} = 72\text{ km/h}$.

questions.question: A bag contains 4 red balls, 5 blue balls, and 3 green balls. Two balls are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both balls are blue?
The perimeter of a rectangle is 68 cm and its length is 6 cm more than its breadth. Find the area of the rectangle.
questions.explanation: $l + b = 34$ and $l - b = 6 \Rightarrow l = 20, b = 14$. Area = $20 \times 14 = 280\text{ cm}^2$.

questions.question: The ratio of present ages of Meena and Seema is $5 : 7$. Four years from now, the sum of their ages will be 56 years. What is Seema's present age?
questions.explanation: Present sum = $56 - 8 = 48$. $5x + 7x = 48 \Rightarrow x = 4$. Seema = $7 \times 4 = 28$ years.

questions.question: Who sits immediately to the right of **A**?
questions.explanation: Unique left-to-right order: **C – G – A – H – D – B – F – E**. Immediately right of A is **H**.

questions.question: Who sits at the **extreme right** end of the row?
questions.explanation: Order: C – G – A – H – D – B – F – **E**. Hence **E** sits at the extreme right end.

questions.question: How many persons sit between **G** and **B**?
questions.explanation: Between G (2nd) and B (6th) sit **A, H, and D** — exactly **Three** persons.

questions.question: What is the position of **D** with respect to **G**?
questions.explanation: G is at position 2 and D is at position 5 ($5 - 2 = 3$), so D is **third to the right** of G.

questions.question: Four of the following five pairs are alike based on their seating positions. Which pair is the odd one out?
questions.explanation: C–A, G–H, A–D, and H–B each have exactly 1 person between them, whereas D–E has 2 persons (B and F) between them.

questions.question: Who sits immediately to the **left** of **P**?
questions.explanation: Counter-clockwise (moving right): P → T → V → Q → S → W → R → U → P. Immediately left of P is **U**.

questions.question: Who sits directly **opposite** to **V**?
questions.explanation: Opposite pairs: P↔S, T↔W, **V↔R**, Q↔U. Hence **R** sits opposite to V.

questions.question: Who sits **second to the right** of **S**?
questions.explanation: Moving right from S: 1st is W, 2nd is **R**.

questions.question: How many persons sit between **T** and **W** when counted from the right of T?
questions.explanation: Moving right from T: V, Q, S sit between T and W (3 persons, since T and W are opposite).

questions.question: Who sits directly **opposite** to **Q**?
questions.explanation: Opposite pairs are P↔S, T↔W, V↔R, and **Q↔U**. Hence **U** is opposite to Q.

questions.question: Who lives on **Floor 2**?
questions.explanation: Floor order (top to bottom): 8-Q, 7-O, 6-L, 5-P, 4-M, 3-J, 2-**N**, 1-K.

questions.question: Who lives on the **topmost floor** (Floor 8)?
questions.explanation: **Q** lives on Floor 8.

questions.question: How many persons live between **L** and **J**?
questions.explanation: L is on Floor 6 and J is on Floor 3; **P (Floor 5) and M (Floor 4)** live between them — **Two** persons.

questions.question: Which floor does **P** live on?
questions.explanation: P lives immediately above M (Floor 4), i.e. on **Floor 5**.

questions.question: Four of the following five live on odd-numbered floors. Who is the odd one out?
questions.explanation: K(1), J(3), P(5), O(7) live on odd floors, while **L** lives on even Floor 6.

questions.question: Which exam is scheduled on **Saturday**?
questions.explanation: Schedule: Mon-Physics, Tue-English, Wed-History, Thu-Maths, Fri-Chemistry, Sat-**Biology**, Sun-Economics.

questions.question: On which day is the **History** exam scheduled?
questions.explanation: History is immediately before Maths (Thursday), so it is on **Wednesday**.

questions.question: How many exams are scheduled between **English** and **Biology**?
questions.explanation: Between Tuesday (English) and Saturday (Biology) are History, Maths, and Chemistry — **Three** exams.

questions.question: Which exam is held immediately **after Chemistry**?
questions.explanation: Chemistry is on Friday, so Saturday's **Biology** exam is immediately after it.

questions.question: If Physics is related to Wednesday and English is related to Thursday in a certain way, then **Maths** is related to which day?
questions.explanation: Each subject maps to 2 days later: Mon+2=Wed, Tue+2=Thu, so Thu(Maths)+2 = **Saturday**.

questions.question:
Statements:
1. Only a few rivers are lakes.
2. All lakes are oceans.

Conclusions:
I. Some rivers are oceans.
II. All rivers can be lakes.
questions.explanation: 'Only a few rivers are lakes' means Some rivers are lakes AND Some rivers are NOT lakes. Hence Some rivers are oceans (I follows), while All rivers can never be lakes (II fails).

questions.question:
Statements:
1. No phone is a tablet.
2. Some tablets are laptops.

Conclusions:
I. Some laptops are not phones.
II. All laptops are phones.
questions.explanation: The portion of laptops that are tablets cannot be phones, so 'Some laptops are not phones' (I) definitely follows.

questions.question:
Statements:
1. Some keys are locks.
2. No lock is a door.

Conclusions:
I. Some keys are doors.
II. No key is a door.
questions.explanation: Neither I nor II follows individually, and 'Some + No' with identical subject-predicate ('keys', 'doors') forms a complementary **Either I or II** pair.

questions.question:
Statements:
1. All trains are tracks.
2. Some tracks are stations.
3. No station is a bus.

Conclusions:
I. Some tracks are not buses.
II. Some trains are stations.
questions.explanation: Tracks that are stations cannot be buses ⇒ I follows. No definite link exists between trains and stations ⇒ II does not follow.

questions.question:
Statement: `P > Q ≥ R = S < T`

Conclusions:
I. `P > S`
II. `Q ≥ T`
options: Either I or II is true
Neither I nor II is true
Both I and II are true
questions.explanation: From `P > Q ≥ R = S`, we definitely get `P > S` (I is true). Between Q and T, signs oppose (`≥` and `<`), so II is false.

questions.question:
Statement: `A ≤ B = C ≤ D < E`

Conclusions:
I. `E > B`
II. `D ≥ A`
options: Either I or II is true
Neither I nor II is true
Both I and II are true
questions.explanation: `B = C ≤ D < E` ⇒ `E > B` (I true). `A ≤ B = C ≤ D` ⇒ `D ≥ A` (II true). Both follow.

questions.question:
Statement: `M ≥ N = O ≥ P`

Conclusions:
I. `M > P`
II. `M = P`
options: Either I or II is true
Neither I nor II is true
Both I and II are true
questions.explanation: The statement gives `M ≥ P`, which splits exactly into `M > P` OR `M = P` ⇒ **Either I or II is true**.

questions.question:
Statements: `K > L ≥ M`; `N ≤ M < O`

Conclusions:
I. `K > N`
II. `O > L`
options: Either I or II is true
Neither I nor II is true
Both I and II are true
questions.explanation: Combined: `K > L ≥ M ≥ N` ⇒ `K > N` (I true). Between O and L: `L ≥ M < O` (opposing signs), so II is false.

questions.question: How is **B** related to **F**?
questions.explanation: B is the wife of A, who is the father of C, and F is C's son. Hence B is F's **Grandmother**.

questions.question: How is **D** related to **G**?
questions.explanation: D is the sister of C (G's father), so D is G's **Paternal Aunt**.

questions.question: How is **E** related to **A**?
questions.explanation: C is A's son and E is C's wife, so E is A's **Daughter-in-law**.

questions.question: What is the shortest distance between Point **X** and Point **Z**?
questions.explanation: X is 6 m North of Y and Z is 8 m East of Y, forming a right triangle: $\sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = 10\text{ m}$.

questions.question: In which direction is Point **X** with respect to Point **W**?
questions.explanation: With Y at $(0,0)$: X is $(0,6)$, Z is $(8,0)$, W is $(8,-6)$. From W to X is West and North ⇒ **North-West**.

questions.question: How many such pairs of letters are there in the word `BANKING` each of which has as many letters between them in the word (in both forward and backward directions) as in the English alphabetical series?
questions.explanation: Positions in BANKING: B(2)-A(1)-N(14)-K(11)-I(9)-N(14)-G(7). Check pairs: (B,A) distance 1 vs |2-1|=1 (1st pair, backward A-B); (I,G) distance 2 vs |9-7|=2 (2nd pair, backward G-I). Total = **Two** pairs.

questions.question: If `1` is added to every even digit and `1` is subtracted from every odd digit in the number `472956`, what is the sum of the 2nd digit from the left and the 2nd digit from the right in the new number?
